es.a3_intro: El trío agregará 432.030 m² entre 2026 y 2028, de los cuales 334.030 m² son orgánicos (6,4% de su GLA total actual; en Chile, 219.900 m², equivalentes al 5,1% del GLA de los principales operadores en Chile y al 6,7% del GLA del propio trío). Las adquisiciones (98.000 m², todas de Parque Arauco) cambian de dueño pero no suman oferta a la industria; por eso el análisis de oferta vs demanda en Chile (Figura 3) usa solo el GLA orgánico.
es.a3_subB: B. GLA POR AÑO DE APERTURA (m²)
es.a3_notaB: Org./GLA = GLA orgánico 2026-2028 sobre GLA consolidado al 2Q26. Mallplaza: el 2028 incluye 46.500 m² de "Otros proyectos Chile", fechados en 2028 por la Memoria 2025 (p.45). Parque Arauco: 2026 = 2S26 (adquisiciones). Cenco: entregas en rango ubicadas al final del rango. En Chile, la oferta orgánica del trío (219.900 m²) equivale al 5,1% del GLA de los principales operadores (≈4,3 millones de m²: 3,29 millones del trío sin oficinas ÷ 76%, su participación en ese universo; no se dispone del GLA total del mercado).
es.a3_fuente: Fuente: Plaza S.A., Release 2Q26 (p.13) y Memoria 2025 (p.45); Parque Arauco, Investor Presentation 2Q26 (slide 23); Cenco Malls, Corporate Presentation 2Q26 (slides 15-17). Solo proyectos con fecha.
es.a4_intro: La ocupación consolidada de los tres operadores se ha mantenido entre 93% y 99% desde el 2T22, incluso durante el ciclo de inflación y tasas altas. Cada empresa define la ocupación de forma distinta, por lo que se comparan tendencias y no niveles.
es.a4_fuente: Fuente: reportes de resultados 2T22-2T26 de las tres empresas. Mallplaza incluye Open Plaza desde el 2T25.
es.a5_intro: El GLA del trío en Chile creció 7,3% desde el 2T22. Mallplaza cedió 1,2 pp de participación porque creció solo con ampliaciones, mientras Parque Arauco sumó Kennedy Oriente (70.000 m²) por compra.
es.a5_sub: A. PARTICIPACIÓN DENTRO DEL TRÍO, 2T22-2T26 (% DEL GLA)
es.a5_fuente: Fuente: reportes de resultados 2T22-2T26 de las tres empresas; análisis del equipo.
es.a6_intro: Industria atractiva: con notas enteras por país ponderadas por el GLA de Mallplaza, la única fuerza intensa es la rivalidad (4), que se da en experiencia y activos y no en precio, ya que en el 2T26 los arriendos en mismas tiendas subieron en Chile en los tres operadores (tabla B).
es.a6_subA: A. NOTAS POR PAÍS Y EVIDENCIA PRINCIPAL (1 = FUERZA DÉBIL; 5 = FUERZA INTENSA)
es.a6_fuenteA: Fuente: análisis del equipo. Nota final = promedio ponderado por GLA de Mallplaza al 2Q26 (Chile 61,9%, Perú 26,2%, Colombia 11,9%), redondeado al entero. En nuevos entrantes el ponderado queda en el límite (1,5) y el equipo lo fija en 2 por las menores barreras de entrada en Perú y Colombia.
es.a6_subB: B. INDICADORES DE PRECIO POR OPERADOR, 2T26
es.a6_fuenteB: Fuente: Plaza S.A., Release 2Q26 (p.18); Cenco Malls, Presentación de Resultados 2T26 (p.17); Parque Arauco, Reporte de Resultados 2T26 (p.5, p.6 y p.21). Cada indicador según la definición de cada empresa: el SSR de Mallplaza considera arriendo fijo de Chile y la variación de la UF; el de Cenco incluye arriendo variable (Cenco 1T26: "SSR Chile acusa el efecto de menores ventas"); el SAR de Parque Arauco mide el arriendo recaudado en áreas arrendadas en ambos períodos. *Incluye gasto común y fondo de promoción: su nivel no es comparable, sí su variación. La variación del ingreso por m² de Mallplaza en Colombia (+8,0%) es cálculo del equipo: 84.790 / 78.545 − 1. Todo lo demás es dato publicado.
a6_evidencia: CR3 76% / 37% / 13%; carrera de reinversión en experiencia; compra de activos (Minka, Plaza Central; anunciadas Quilín y Chicureo); oferta que alcanza al consumo en 2027. Participaciones estables y márgenes de 71-90%. Sin guerra de precios: SSR/SAR positivos en Chile (tabla B).
Capital intensivo (USD 613 MM por 170.200 m² en Mallplaza); bancos de terrenos de incumbentes; Perú y Colombia menos concentrados; Colombia con mayoría de malls en propiedad horizontal.
Ocupación Chile 96-99%; contratos de 5,0-8,7 años promedio; top 5 = 18% de ingresos de Mallplaza; SSR Chile sobre IPC (6,9% vs 4,8%, 1T23-2T26); tiendas por departamento 19,0% del GLA.
Gasto común traspasado al locatario (Memoria 2025, nota 2.20); costo de ventas 6,2% de ingresos de Mallplaza.
93% del ingreso por arriendo de Mallplaza es fijo; visitas 2T26 +4,4% Chile, +1,3% Perú, +2,5% Colombia; giro a experiencia. Sin datos oficiales de e-commerce por país.

Datos de empresas al 30-jun-2026; proyecciones macro del IPoM de septiembre 2026 por ser las vigentes más recientes.

en.a3_intro: The trio will add 432,030 m² between 2026 and 2028, of which 334,030 m² are organic (6.4% of their current total GLA; in Chile, 219,900 m², equivalent to 5.1% of the main operators' GLA in Chile and 6.7% of the trio's own GLA). Acquisitions (98,000 m², all by Parque Arauco) change owner but add no supply to the industry; the supply-versus-demand analysis for Chile (Figure 3) therefore uses organic GLA only.
en.a3_notaB: Org./GLA = organic GLA 2026-2028 over consolidated GLA at 2Q26. Mallplaza: 2028 includes 46,500 m² of “Other projects Chile”, dated 2028 by the 2025 Annual Report (p.45). Parque Arauco: 2026 = 2H26 (acquisitions). Cenco: deliveries given as a range are placed at the end of the range. In Chile, the trio's organic supply (219,900 m²) equals 5.1% of the main operators' GLA (≈4.3 million m²: 3.29 million of the trio excluding offices ÷ 76%, its share of that universe; total market GLA is not available).
en.a3_fuente: Source: Plaza S.A., 2Q26 Release (p.13) and 2025 Annual Report (p.45); Parque Arauco, 2Q26 Investor Presentation (slide 23); Cenco Malls, 2Q26 Corporate Presentation (slides 15-17). Dated projects only.
en.a4_intro: The consolidated occupancy of the three operators has stayed between 93% and 99% since 2Q22, even through the inflation and high-rate cycle. Each company defines occupancy differently, so trends are compared rather than levels.
en.a4_fuente: Source: 2Q22-2Q26 earnings reports of the three companies. Mallplaza includes Open Plaza since 2Q25.
en.a5_intro: The trio's GLA in Chile grew 7.3% since 2Q22. Mallplaza gave up 1.2 pp of share because it grew only through expansions, while Parque Arauco added Kennedy Oriente (70,000 m²) by purchase.
en.a5_sub: A. SHARE WITHIN THE TRIO, 2Q22-2Q26 (% OF GLA)
en.a5_fuente: Source: 2Q22-2Q26 earnings reports of the three companies; Team analysis.
en.a6_intro: Attractive industry: with whole-number scores by country weighted by Mallplaza's GLA, the only intense force is rivalry (4), which plays out in experience and assets rather than price, since in 2Q26 same-store rents rose in Chile at all three operators (table B).
en.a6_subA: A. SCORES BY COUNTRY AND MAIN EVIDENCE (1 = WEAK FORCE; 5 = INTENSE FORCE)
en.a6_fuenteA: Source: Team analysis. Final score = average weighted by Mallplaza's GLA at 2Q26 (Chile 61.9%, Peru 26.2%, Colombia 11.9%), rounded to the nearest integer. For new entrants the weighted score sits at the threshold (1.5) and the team sets it at 2 because of lower entry barriers in Peru and Colombia.
en.a6_fuenteB: Source: Plaza S.A., 2Q26 Release (p.18); Cenco Malls, 2Q26 Earnings Presentation (p.17); Parque Arauco, 2Q26 Earnings Report (p.5, p.6 and p.21). Each indicator follows each company's definition: Mallplaza's SSR considers fixed rent in Chile and the change in the UF; Cenco's includes variable rent (Cenco 1Q26: “SSR Chile reflects the effect of lower sales”); Parque Arauco's SAR measures rent collected in areas leased in both periods. *Includes common expenses and promotion fund: its level is not comparable, its change is. Mallplaza's revenue per m² change in Colombia (+8.0%) is a team calculation: 84,790 / 78,545 − 1. Everything else is published data.
a6_evidencia: CR3 76% / 37% / 13%; reinvestment race in experience; asset purchases (Minka, Plaza Central; Quilín and Chicureo announced); supply catching up with consumption in 2027. Stable shares and margins of 71-90%. No price war: positive SSR/SAR in Chile (table B).
Capital intensive (USD 613 million for 170,200 m² at Mallplaza); incumbents' land banks; Peru and Colombia less concentrated; Colombia with most malls under horizontal ownership.
Chile occupancy 96-99%; contracts averaging 5.0-8.7 years; top 5 = 18% of Mallplaza's revenue; Chile SSR above CPI (6.9% vs 4.8%, 1Q23-2Q26); department stores 19.0% of GLA.
Common expenses passed through to tenants (2025 Annual Report, note 2.20); cost of sales 6.2% of Mallplaza's revenue.
93% of Mallplaza's rental income is fixed; 2Q26 visits +4.4% Chile, +1.3% Peru, +2.5% Colombia; shift to experience. No official e-commerce data by country.
en.a7_intro: Criteria used so that figures are comparable across operators and consistent with the official 2Q26 reports.
a7_textos: Measured by GLA (not by sales) over each country's main operators (slide 7, 2Q26 Institutional Presentation). Partial HHI: considers only the operators identified on slide 7, so it is a floor (the real HHI is equal or higher); classified with the 2023 DOJ/FTC Merger Guidelines thresholds (above 1,800 = highly concentrated). Colombia pro forma: includes Gran Plaza (announced acquisition of 179,667 m²; 2Q26 Release); without it, Mallplaza's share would be 4.3%.
Only dated projects in official reports at 2Q26 and the 2025 Annual Report; dates given as a range are placed at the end of the range; acquisitions are not new supply for the industry.

Chile only and only m² that depend on consumption (excludes offices and multifamily); base GLA excludes Cenco's offices. Private consumption from the September 2026 IPoM is used as a demand indicator, not as a sales projection. Main-operators GLA in Chile ≈ trio GLA excluding offices ÷ 76% (the trio's share of that universe, slide 7); total market GLA is not available, and the trio's supply is a lower bound of the industry's supply.

EBITDA per each company's definition (none includes the IAS 40 revaluation); 2Q26 EBITDA not annualized; GLA consolidated at 100% of controlled assets. Parque Arauco: multifamily NOI (CLP 503 million) is subtracted, since its size is reported in units and not in m²; effect −0.7%, does not change the ranking.

Profile and duration weighted by GLA. Cenco states it explicitly; Parque Arauco presents its maturity profile as % of GLA but does not state the basis of its average duration; Mallplaza does not publish the basis. In both cases GLA is assumed.
Tenant sales in Chile 2Q26 vs 2Q25 deflated with the 12-month CPI of June 2026 (4.3%; INE, release of 08-07-2026). Cenco 2Q25 calculated from its published change (−1.9%).

InRetail 2Q26 adjusted EBITDA, Shopping Malls segment (S/ 131 million; excludes investment property revaluation) ÷ total GLA of 888,000 m² (InRetail, 2Q26 Corporate Presentation, p.26 and p.29). Mallplaza Peru: published monthly EBITDA per m² (S/ 53) × 3 (2Q26 Release, p.18). Margins are not compared: InRetail calculates its own on net rent.
Company data as of 30-Jun-2026; macro projections from the September 2026 IPoM as the most recent available.
